note: The sensible bot (tools/bot.mjs) on seeds 1-3 for 8 sim hours (about three and a half game days: the clock runs 6 to 60 times faster than the sim, src/sim/day.ts) from a fresh game. Proposed from the first run on 8 Oct 2026 at 48 game hours and re-proposed on 8 Oct 2026 when sim seconds became real seconds (the clock six times faster than motion): the same money a real minute, but a quicker start and fewer lost, since a peak lasts a sixth of the sim seconds it did while patience and platform caps are in sim seconds; and lost re-proposed on 11 Oct 2026 when trains began boarding through their stop (two doors a car, 0.7 passengers a second each) instead of all at once on arrival: people who reach the platform while a train stands now catch it, so Stockport's queue rarely reaches its cap and lost fell from about 155 to 30 while cash and milestones stayed in range. Re-proposed again on 11 Oct 2026 when stations began as halts (the owner's decision): Stockport's subway, platform 3 and booking hall come before the second unit (0.17 to 0.4 h), so Heaton Chapel comes later (0.4 to 0.72 h) and everything after a little later; stages cost money, so less cash at the end; and peaks bite again (lost 30 to 205), as the second unit arrives later and Stockport's subway brings more people in. Lost re-proposed on 12 Oct 2026 when demand came from door-to-door journey times (docs/DESIGN.md, Journeys): each group draws its own time budget and gives up when its wait has used what's left, so the peaks press on Heaton Chapel and Levenshulme too when full trains leave Stockport (205 to about 350, a third of it beyond Stockport); demand is scaled so the milestones stay where they were (Heaton Chapel 0.72 to 0.65 h, Ardwick 5.55 to 5.2 h). Re-proposed on 12 October 2026 when trains began running to a timetable (docs/DESIGN.md, Timetable): the units now keep an even gap instead of running wherever they were added, so waits are what the journeys assume and far fewer give up (lost about 350 to 80, nearly all at Stockport's first morning, before the second unit); stops overrun when a crowded train meets a crowded platform, but by the second morning the bot's line has the room, so its trains run at most half a minute late. The bot also buys the faster timetable once it has £45,000 spare (a player would, rather than sit on the money), which takes about £20,000 off cash at the end on main too; cash at the end re-proposed to 25,000-55,000 for both. New measures: the share of main-line departures within five minutes of the timetable, the worst lateness in minutes, and the longest daytime quiet (06:00-22:00 with nothing bought, 0.7 h on main). Lost re-proposed on 12 October 2026 when the peaks were made to press again (docs/DESIGN.md, Journeys and Platforms; the owner asked for pressure at the stations they buy): no grace past the budget, and a wait past the timetabled gap felt at three times riding, with demand 1.9 to 1.95 so the milestones stay where they were; lost about 80 to 200, nearly 40% of it beyond Stockport (a new measure, lost beyond home %, 33-100; 11, 8 and 12% on seeds 1-3 before), most at Heaton Chapel and Levenshulme in the second morning. Platforms now block, but on the bot's line never engage. The owner agrees ranges when the pacing is settled. `ok` is inside the range, `near` within 15% of it, `off` beyond. Lost and lost beyond home % re-proposed on 12 October 2026 when taxi ranks came (docs/DESIGN.md, Taxi ranks): a share of those who give up at a station with a rank take a cab while one's in, counted as by cab rather than lost, so lost falls (about 200 to 140) and more of it is Stockport's first morning, before the bot can afford a rank (beyond home 38 to 28%); lost re-proposed as 120-300 and beyond home as 25-100, and by cab added at 15-60 (about 32). The bot buys a rank once a dozen have given up at a station, so Stockport's comes just after the second unit and Heaton Chapel a little later (0.65 to 0.75 h). Things going wrong came on 12 October 2026 (docs/DESIGN.md, Things going wrong): failed trains and signal failures from the second sim hour, one or two in 8 sim hours, with replacement buses and a spare unit the bot buys once a train has failed. The milestones held; what moved is where trouble lands, the second morning's peak on seeds 2 and 3, mostly as Stockport's platform fills behind a held train: lost 139 to about 210 (seed 2's two failed trains 300), cash 50,800 to about 40,300, worst late up to 8 minutes, and lost beyond home 28 to 23%, so that range is re-proposed as 15-100. New measures, proposed: failures 0-3 and signal failures 0-3 a run, and lost in trouble (who gave up while something was wrong or in the quarter hour after) 0-200. Trouble softened the same day: nothing starts where it would still be going in a peak's busiest hour (troubleCalm, 06:30-08:30 and 16:00-18:00 by the clock), as seed 2 lost 162 people and seed 11 a quarter of its takings to failures in the second morning. On seeds 1-12 the most any seed earns less than the same seed with no trouble is 8.5% of its cash at the end (25.6% before); on seeds 1-3 lost in trouble 1, 162, 81 to 1, 42, 33 and cash 40,300 to 48,600 on average (seed 2 still buys the spare unit after its one failure). Lost in trouble re-proposed as 0-150 (124 the most on seeds 1-12). Homes and draw came from Census 2021 the same day (docs/DESIGN.md, Homes and draw), scaled so Stockport's morning trips to Piccadilly are as before; Stockport's real draw is half the guess and Piccadilly's homes well under it, so the evenings earned less and Levenshulme slipped past the first night (2.3 to 4.0 h), and fareMult went from 12 to 13.5 to bring it back (2.6 h). Heaton Chapel 0.75 to 0.63 h, Ardwick 4.9 to 4.8 h, lost about the same (150 to 193), and cash at the end 48,600 to 58,600 with the dearer fares, so cash at the end is re-proposed as 25,000-65,000. Homes that grow came on 12 October 2026 (docs/DESIGN.md, Homes that grow): each owned station's homes grow towards a ceiling from the census at 6% of the gap a sim hour times the reach of its trip, and demand reads them. Growth at 12% took cash at the end to 73,500 (off), so it was halved to keep the opening as it was: on seeds 1-3 Levenshulme 2.6 h (as before), Ardwick 4.8 to 5.0 h (seed 1's one failed train lands in the second morning now, 5.5 h), cash 58,600 to 55,500, boarded 4,630 to 4,660, lost 193 to 280 (seed 1's failure, 408; seeds 2 and 3 235 and 198); on seeds 1-12 the means move little (Levenshulme 2.9 to 2.7 h, cash 54,400 to 58,800, lost 189 to 221, lost in trouble 30 to 48). Over 30 sim hours Piccadilly comes at 8.6-9.3 h (9.2 h before) and Hazel Grove at 13.6-13.8 h (14.0 h). New measure, homes grown (homes over the census catchments at the end, about 130 in 8 sim hours, 580 in 30), proposed as 80-200. Weather and seasons came on 12 October 2026 (docs/DESIGN.md, Weather and seasons): spells from the weather's own seeded random numbers, so the rest of the game's dice are as they were (the bot's --fair, the weather unfelt, matches main exactly); rain makes the walk and an open wait feel a little longer, snow slows the line and keeps a few at home, leaves slow autumn's trains. The first game day stays dry, as rain in seed 2's first evening took Levenshulme past the first night (2.62 to 3.75 h); with it dry the milestones hold on seeds 1-3 (Ardwick 5.0 to 4.8 h, as seed 1's failed train no longer lands in the second morning), cash 55,500 to 62,300, lost 280 to 209. On seeds 1-12 boarded 4,730 to 4,721 and cash 58,800 to 61,100 (where trouble lands moves more than the rain). Over 32 sim hours, a whole year, cash at the end is 6% under the same seeds unfelt and boarded 4%, wet about a fifth of the time. New measure, wet hours (sim hours of rain or snow), proposed as 0-2.5 in 8 sim hours (1.0, 0.48, 0.48 on seeds 1-3). Every platform in use came on 12 October 2026 (docs/DESIGN.md, Platforms and Expresses): each service takes the platforms it really uses, a turning list shared out by unit (the stoppers turn in Stockport's 4 and 3 by turns), and Avanti West Coast and CrossCountry call at Stockport once platform 3 is built and pay an access charge (£40) and £2 a long-distance passenger. Against main with the weather, on seeds 1-3: Levenshulme 2.6 to 2.5 h, Ardwick 4.8 h as before, lost 209 to 180, and cash at the end 62,300 to 65,900, just over its range (the expresses pay about £3,000 of it, and buy Levenshulme a little sooner), so cash at the end is re-proposed as 25,000-70,000; the trains' platforms change nothing else the bot sees, as the units keep their gap. New measures, proposed: express £ (what the expresses paid) 2,000-5,000, and through (long-distance passengers on and off at owned stations) 500-1,200. Car parks and bus links came on 12 October 2026 (docs/DESIGN.md, Car parks and bus links): the census's pools beyond a walk travel by car or bus once a car park or bus link is built, and the bot buys them before a morning once it has twice the price. Nothing changes until one is built (the milestones to Levenshulme are as on main); in 8 sim hours the bot builds Levenshulme's bus stop and car park in the second morning and Stockport's car park in the third, so Ardwick comes a little later (4.8 to 5.1 h), cash at the end falls (65,900 to 39,200, the money in car parks), boarded rises (4,770 to 4,830) and the longest quiet stretch shortens (2.1 to 1.5 h, so that range is re-proposed as 1.2-2.7). New measures, proposed: by car (drivers who parked) 30-200 and by bus link 20-150. Shorter days, quick nights came on 12 October 2026 (the owner: the day/night cycle was long and the night pointless to wait through; docs/DESIGN.md, Numbers that matter, Time): the clock keeps its rate through the peaks (06:00-09:30, 16:00-19:00), runs twice as fast between them and passes the night (23:00-05:00) in about two real minutes, so a game day is 45 real minutes at 1x instead of 80, and each clock hour carries the trips it did. 8 sim hours are now 3.42 game days instead of 2, so the milestones come sooner in sim hours (Levenshulme 2.47 to 1.93 h, Ardwick 5.1 to 3.3, and Piccadilly within the run at 5.9 h) and every total is bigger; not re-priced, as waiting less is the point. Like for like over the first two game days on seeds 1-3, earned a game day is 137,400 against 140,900 (2.5% less: fewer trains a clock hour between the peaks), homes grown 128 against 131, by car and by bus link as before, and lost 191, 341, 194 against 172, 217, 205 (seed 2's two failed trains 179 of its 341; outside trouble 134, 162, 125 against 111, 143, 140). With the old rate from 06:30 rather than 06:00, Stockport stranded about 30 more each second morning. Re-proposed from the 8-hour run: Ardwick 2.6-4.2, Piccadilly 4.5-8, cash at the end 20,000-120,000, boarded 10,000-17,000, lost 400-900, by cab 80-200, longest quiet hours 0.5-1.6 (the night is short now), longest daytime quiet 0.3-1.2, worst late min 0-12, failures 0-4, lost in trouble 0-550 (seed 3's three failed trains, 498), homes grown 180-340, express £ 4,500-8,500, through 1,300-2,500, by car 300-650, by bus link 100-260; new measure, game days 3.3-3.6 (the bot also reports earned and lost a game day). The expresses came onto the clock on 12 October 2026 (docs/DESIGN.md, Expresses): one of each every two clock hours from about 06:00 to 23:00, two units a service taking the slots by turns, as their slots in sim seconds had left a quarter fewer a game day after shorter days. Over the first two game days on seeds 1-3 express £ is 2,864, 2,860, 2,860 (2,212, 2,216, 2,212 before; 2,991 before shorter days); over 8 sim hours express £ 6,490 to 8,077 and through 1,879 to 2,232 a seed on average, so they are re-proposed as 5,500-10,500 and 1,600-2,900. The milestones hold (Ardwick 3.3 to 3.1 h); lost 605 to 717, as an express standing in platform 3 more often holds a stopper behind it in the peaks. The bot also reports express £ and calls a game day and cash a game day. Real last and first trains came the same day (docs/DESIGN.md, Timetable): the stoppers run 05:30 to 23:30 and stand at the ends of their runs overnight, the timetable starting fresh each morning, and people who come after the last train give up. Seeds 1-3: Levenshulme 1.92 h as before, Ardwick 3.13 to 3.35 h, Piccadilly 5.78 to 5.82 h, lost 717 to 838 (seed 2 1,171 with two failed trains in the peaks, 502 of it lost in trouble; seeds 4-9 626 to 701), boarded 13,804 to 13,398, cash at the end 63,400 to 50,000. New measure, lost after the last train (who gave up between 23:30 and midnight), proposed as 0-40 (11, 8, 10).

long.note: The late game, proposed 13 October 2026 when the Buxton line came (docs/ROADMAP.md, phase 5 step 2): the bot on seeds 1-3 for 16 sim hours (about seven game days), held to these ranges when run with --hours 16. The 8-hour run never reaches Hazel Grove, so it plays exactly as before (every measure identical to main on seeds 1-3); over 16 hours Hazel Grove comes at 8.4-9.3 h as before, then Middlewood at 10.3-10.5 h, Disley at 12.2-12.5 h and New Mills Newtown at 14.8-15.0 h, priced on from Hazel Grove's 200,000 at 280,000, 380,000 and 500,000. They fill the late game's quiet: the longest stretch with nothing to buy falls from 4.9, 2.6 and 3.0 h to 1.1, 1.6 and 1.4 h, and the longest daytime one from 2.0 h to 1.1-1.5 h. The branch's one unit runs further as each is bought, so its trains come less often: earned a game day 2% under main (341,000 against 353,000 on average), the new stations small (Middlewood 34 homes, Disley 50, New Mills Newtown 9, most of New Mills taking New Mills Central). Re-proposed the same day when the Marple line came (phase 5 step 3): Ashburys comes after Hazel Grove beside Middlewood, and the bot buys the cheaper of the two lines' next stations, so Middlewood (280,000) at 10.3-10.5 h as before, then Ashburys (300,000) at 11.8-12.2 h and Belle Vue (340,000) at 13.7-13.8 h, before Disley (380,000) at 15.7-15.9 h (seed 2 not within 16 h); New Mills Newtown and the rest of the Marple line come after 16 h. Earned a game day is as before (339,000-345,000); more give up a game day (525-760 against 370-540), at the new stations and where the Marple trains turn in Piccadilly's platform 5 beside the stopper until Piccadilly's platforms are built (which the bot never buys), and the worst late running rises to 9.5-17 minutes. Re-proposed the same day when places came (docs/design/buying.md, phase 5 step 13a): stations are offered by touching, and the bot saves for the offered station with the most homes and draw per pound, which keeps the 8-hour run exactly as before (PLAY identical on seeds 1-3 with the save version held) but after Hazel Grove takes the Marple line first: Ashburys (433 homes and draw for 300,000) at 10.3-10.6 h where Middlewood (49 for 280,000) came at 10.3-10.5, then Belle Vue at 12.0-12.4 h and Ryder Brow at 14.1-14.5 h; Middlewood and Disley come after 16 h. The pace of a new station every two hours or so holds, as do the quiet stretches (longest 1.3-1.8 h, daytime 1.0-1.2 h). Re-proposed 14 October 2026 with frequencies to buy (docs/briefs/services.md, part b): the bot buys a branch's next frequency step once it runs to three stations and there's three times its price, the Hazel Grove line's second unit at 7.9-8.3 h and the Marple line's at 13.3-13.6 h, so Hazel Grove comes at 9.3-9.7 h (from 8.7-9.4), Ashburys 10.9-11.5 h and Ryder Brow at 15.5-16.0 h (from 14.7-15.1), past the old 15.5: Ryder Brow's range goes to 13-16.5. Boarded over 16 h rises about 4% (42,200-42,900 from 40,400-41,900) as the second units shorten the branches' waits.

contract.note: Contract renewal (docs/DESIGN.md, Contract renewal), proposed 12 October 2026: the bot on seeds 1-3 with --runs 2 renews as soon as it owns Piccadilly, banks the reputation and buys perks in its order (tools/bot.mjs, PERKS), then plays the same seed again with them. A first run banks 62, 62, 64 and buys Framework contractor, Signposting and A unit in the sidings; the second run reaches Piccadilly at 4.08, 4.07, 4.82 h against 5.82, 5.92, 5.85 (26% sooner, the brief's target being about a quarter), Heaton Chapel at 0.25 h against 0.63 and Levenshulme at 0.98 against 1.93. A run with no perks plays exactly as before. Renewing as soon as it can banks less each time (quicker runs carry fewer people), so five contracts in a row level off at 3.6 h to Piccadilly (39% sooner) with Heaton Chapel at 0.17 h.
